question: During both Shaolin trip and Mongolian trip, the streamer mentioned the temperature at that time. Which place had a lower temperature, and what exactly was the degree?

db_evidence.notes: The DB does contain temperature facts for both trips. Shaolin: topic_facts at time_s 203258 and episode captions at 206348-206408 both consistently say 'around 20 degrees' -- this matches the reference and all rollouts got it right. Mongolia: there are THREE distinct temperature mentions across the trip -- (1) time_s 339744, 'temperature is minus 17 degrees outside in mongolia' (near trip arrival, ~6h before the clue interval), (2) time_s 345954 ('episodes:30sec:011539', topic_facts:00008603), 'he notes that it's only six or seven degrees outside and extremely cold' -- this episode's 30sec window (345954-345984) contains the question's logical clue_interval [345959,345964] almost exactly, but the caption text is POSITIVE ('six or seven degrees') with no negative sign, unlike the reference answer of -6, and (3) time_s 346284, 'the snowy mongolian weather and the minus-five-degree celsius temperature' -- close in time to the clue interval and negative, but off by one from -6 and ~330s later than the clue window. Mention (1) is the only one any semantic_search(topic_facts, ...) call ever surfaced in its top-10 results across all 5 rollouts; mentions (2) and (3), despite being the temporally correct ones per the clue_interval, never appeared in any rollout's tool outputs. Mention (2) is likely the ground-truth event but its caption appears to have dropped a negative sign (a plausible ASR/captioning error, since '-5' and '-6/-7' bracket the reference's -6 within the same short stretch of footage), so even a rollout that found it would need real audio verification (clip_qa) to recover the correct signed value.

root_causes: semantic_search(topic_facts, 'Mongolia(n) trip temperature degrees') deterministically returns the -17°C arrival-temperature fact as the single highest-scoring hit in all 5 rollouts, crowding out the later, question-relevant temperature mentions from ever appearing in the top-10 results.

No rollout issued a SQL scan across the FULL Mongolia trip time range (~339684-354024) specifically filtering for 'degree'/'temperature' text; SQL follow-ups all stayed narrowly centered on the already-found -17°C timestamp (e.g. 339650-339850), so the true clue-adjacent facts at 345954 and 346284 were never queried even though they were reachable with a simple ILIKE '%degree%' scan (as this diagnosis's own sql check found in one query).

One rollout (rollout-02) did use clip_qa/visual-verification, but only to confirm the already-chosen -17°C candidate rather than to search for other temperature mentions in the trip -- verification was applied to the wrong candidate, not used to discover the right one.

Possible caption/ASR error in the underlying memory DB: the clue-interval fact (345954, 'six or seven degrees') is captioned as positive rather than negative, which would have misled even a rollout that found it toward a wrong-signed answer without further audio verification via clip_qa.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly retrieved and reported the Shaolin temperature (~20°C), which does match both the topic_facts entry and the episode captions at the clue interval.
All 5 rollouts correctly identified the direction of the comparison (Mongolia is colder than Shaolin).
rollout-02 correctly used clip_qa to verify a claimed spoken quote against source audio/video before submitting, which is good practice even though it verified the wrong candidate here.
transferable_lessons: When a question says 'during the trip, X mentioned Y', do not stop at the single highest-scoring semantic_search hit for Y -- a long trip segment (hours) can contain multiple mentions of the same attribute (temperature) at different times, and only the specific one near the question's implicit context is correct.

After semantic_search finds one candidate fact, run a broad SQL scan (ILIKE '%degree%' or similar) across the ENTIRE relevant episode/trip time range, not just a narrow window around the first hit, to check for competing/later mentions of the same attribute.

Use clip_qa/visual-verification to disambiguate BETWEEN multiple candidate mentions of an attribute, not just to confirm the first candidate found -- verification should target uncertainty about which mention is relevant, not just whether the chosen one is real.

Be suspicious of captions describing a quantity without a sign (e.g. 'six or seven degrees' with no explicit 'minus') when temporally close to other captions in the same DB that do carry a negative sign for the same location/context (e.g. 'minus-five-degree celsius' 330s later) -- this pattern suggests an ASR/captioning error dropping a negative sign, and should trigger a clip_qa audio check rather than being read as ground truth.
open_questions: Was the streamer's actual spoken value in the source video near time_s 345954-345984 really '-6 degrees' (matching the reference) or something else -- this diagnosis did not pull frames/audio to directly verify the clue-interval quote, relying instead on the DB caption text ('six or seven degrees') and the nearby 346284 caption ('minus-five-degree celsius') as circumstantial evidence of a sign-dropping caption error.

Why does semantic_search over topic_facts for a generic query like 'Mongolia temperature degrees' consistently rank the arrival-temperature fact above the clue-interval fact -- is this due to embedding similarity favoring 'temperature'+'mongolia' co-occurring explicitly in the fact text (339744's fact literally contains 'in mongolia') while the clue fact's text does not mention 'mongolia' explicitly?
